newsitem.title: USA: 3 arrested in FBI van theft, most weapons recovered.
newsitem.headline: 3 arrested in FBI van theft, most weapons recovered.

text.p: Memphis police Thursday arrested three suspects and recovered nearly all of the high-tech weapons that were taken when an FBI van was stolen this week, FBI Director Louis Freeh said.

Freeh told the House Judiciary subcommittee on crime that police in Memphis had arrested three people and were questioning others about the incident, which began when the GMC Suburban van was stolen from a parking lot of a hotel where a visiting team of FBI agents from Little Rock, Arkansas, spent Monday night.

The burned-out SWAT van was found early Tuesday on the northern edge of Memphis but a dozen assault weapons including automatic assault rifles, tear gas canisters, several grenade launchers and 8,000 rounds of ammunition were missing.

Freeh said all the arms except for a single grenade launcher had now been recovered. But he was pressured by one member of the panel to fire or suspend the "knucklehead" FBI agents who left the van full of weapons unattended.

"Is this comic strip time or something?" asked Representative John Conyers, a Democrat, who urged Freeh to suspend or fire the agents involved in order "to send a message to any other knuckleheads out there."

Some members of the panel called on Attorney General Janet Reno to investigate the FBI's policies on weapons handling, asking incredulously how a SWAT van without special locks or an alarm system and full of sophisticated weapons could be left unattended in a hotel parking lot.

Tennessee Democrat Harold Ford said the incident raised serious questions about the FBI's procedures. "I find it extremely troubling that a mistake of this magnitude would ever occur. In light of this apparent negligence, a thorough investigation of this matter is warranted," he said.
Reno expressed concern about the incident at her weekly Justice Department news conference. "I'm troubled when an FBI van is stolen and weapons are taken and the FBI van is destroyed," she said.

"The FBI is reviewing all the processes and procedures in place to see what must be done to address this problem," she said. "We're reviewing it to see what happened, to see if we need to impose new procedures or to take other action."

Freeh told the committee he wanted to be fair to the agents involved and "get all the facts together" before dismissing or suspending anybody. "This is a very serious matter. If we don't have rules and regulations, we will very quickly," he said.
